subject: ZenHealth: Cross-border data transfer clarification and evidence request
messages:
From: Zena Patel <zena.patel@zenhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@zenhealth.com>, security@zenhealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Cross-border transfer details for ZenHealth vendor review

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this — ZenHealth is kicking off a vendor TIA for providers who will process EU/UK personal data. We’re compiling a short packet to share with our Data Protection team. For Redwood, can you please confirm the following and share any supporting evidence (SCC Annex, SOC 2 report, dataflow map) where possible: 

- Which legal mechanism(s) do you rely on for transfers from the EU/UK to the U.S. (e.g., SCCs, adequacy, other)?
- Are the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) implemented verbatim or with Annexes/technical measures? If SCCs, can you provide the signed Annex?
- Do you maintain a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) or DPIA covering hosted inference? If so, can you provide a redacted summary?
- Data categories and typical retention windows (particularly logs, request/response content, embeddings).
- Subprocessor list and any known cross-border subprocessors outside the US/EU.
- Evidence of technical controls for cross-border risk mitigation (encryption in transit/at rest, key management, access controls).

If you can send the materials by EOD Tuesday (3 business days), that would help our submission timeline. If there are items you cannot share publicly, we can accept a secure link or NDA redaction. 

Appreciate it — happy to set a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Zena Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy
ZenHealth
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Zena Patel <zena.patel@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border transfer details for ZenHealth vendor review

Hi Zena —

Thanks for the clear list. I’m attaching an initial package and summarizing answers inline to help your DPIA/TIA: 

1) Legal mechanism: Redwood relies on the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (processor-to-processor / processor-to-controller as applicable) as the primary legal mechanism for transfers from the EU/UK to the U.S. We also support contractual commitments in our DPA for customers who require data residency or Private deployment options.

2) SCCs & Annexes: We have implemented the SCCs and provide a signed customer Annex with our DPA. Attached: "Redwood_SCC_Annex.pdf" (redacted where necessary) — if you need the full executed Annex we can coordinate a secure exchange or NDA.

3) TIA/DPIA: Redwood maintains internal Transfer Impact Assessments and product DPIA summaries for hosted inference. For confidentiality we’re providing a redacted summary in the attached package and an internal dataflow map (redwood_dataflow_map_v3.zip). If ZenHealth needs a deeper copy or a live walkthrough, we can schedule a call and/or provide a redacted PDF.

4) Data categories & retention: Typical categories include request metadata, request/response text (customer-controlled; retention configurable), embeddings (if enabled by customer), and logs/metrics. Default retention windows: request logs and observability traces = 30 days; audit logs = 365 days; customer-specified artifacts (models, snapshots) retained per contract. We do not use customer input for model training unless explicitly permitted.

5) Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor list; most subprocessors are in the US and EU. We’ll share the current list via the secure Drive link included below.

6) Technical controls: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, tenant isolation in our runtime, KMS integration for customer-managed keys (available in Private), role-based access controls, and SOC2 Type II controls over our environment. Attached: "SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf" (summary) and the dataflow map.

Next steps: I’ve attached the three items above. If ZenHealth’s Data Protection team needs a short call to review the redacted DPIA and Annex, Vanessa (cc’d) can coordinate a 30-minute slot next week. 

Notes on mitigations and fallback: We offer Dedicated and Private deployment options for customers seeking to avoid cross-border transfers altogether; we can discuss cost/ops tradeoffs if that’s required.

Best regards,

Priyom Das
Senior Security Product Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SCC_Annex.pdf (redacted), SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf (summary), redwood_dataflow_map_v3.zip

Hi Priyom —

Received, and thanks for the quick package. A couple follow-ups from the ZenHealth Privacy team: 

- Can you confirm whether the default logging/observability captures any personal identifiers and whether those logs are pseudonymized or encrypted at rest? 
- Does Redwood maintain an internal DPIA for the hosted inference product that we can rely on (we don’t need full raw assets, a signed redacted summary is ideal)?
- We’re particularly interested in the specifics of key management for customer data in hosted mode (who holds keys by default; is CMK available to customers?).

If you can provide those clarifications before EOD Wednesday, that helps our risk acceptance timeline. Also looping in Tom (privacy lead) in case he has technical follow-ups. 

Thanks —
Zena
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Zena Patel <zena.patel@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 15:03:00 -08:00

Hi Zena and Tom —

Quick answers inline to your clarifying questions and a proposed next step: 

- Logging & identifiers: Default observability logs capture request metadata (timestamps, route, model id, request size, client id) but do not persist PII fields by default. Request/response content is stored per customer configuration; customers can opt out of request retention. For logs that could contain identifiers, we pseudonymize identifiable fields and encrypt logs at rest (AES-256).

- DPIA: Redwood has an internal DPIA for hosted inference. We can provide a signed redacted summary suitable for vendor reviews; I’ve included a one-page extract below and we can provide a redacted PDF on request or arrange a secure review with our Privacy team.

- Key management: By default Redwood manages encryption keys in our KMS (controls accessible to our infra team). For customers requiring additional isolation, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integration in Dedicated/Private deployments; we document CMK options in the DPA and in deployment runbooks.

Attached again: redwood_dataflow_map_v3.zip and a short DPIA extract (redacted). Vanessa will reach out to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough — please let us know 2-3 slots that work next week.

If you prefer, we can also provide a short questionnaire response with checkboxes for your TIA template to expedite sign-off.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Security Product Manager
Redwood Inference
